artifacts.summary: Resolves all five dispatch design questions for the /tag branch-reachability gate: REFUSE (not auto-push), placed in Step 2, using the ahead rev-list count (proven mathematically equivalent to the CI's merge-base predicate since /tag always tags HEAD), no override flag, plus a documented non-goal for the never-pushed-branch edge case.

memory_candidates.content: When a shell skill always operates on HEAD with no commit-ish argument (verified by grep for the git command's argument list), a symmetric 'ahead' rev-list count (git rev-list --count origin/branch..HEAD) is not a proxy/approximation for a CI ancestry gate (git merge-base --is-ancestor HEAD origin/branch) -- it is mathematically identical to it. Prefer the cheap rev-list count (reusable, gives an integer for messaging) over an extra merge-base call, but record the HEAD-only invariant explicitly since it's what makes the equivalence hold.

Design pattern for deciding whether a validation gate needs a --skip-* override flag: grant an override only when the failure can reflect a legitimate judgment call the operator is entitled to make differently (e.g. a version/changelog mismatch during an unusual release). Refuse to add an override when the only remedy is a single safe, no-judgment command and bypassing it would directly reproduce the exact incident the gate exists to prevent (e.g. pushing a branch before tagging it) -- an override flag there just hands back the footgun.
